title: feat(spec): row-level declarative field write — operation: 'update' + patch on ActionSchema
body:
Fixes #14092

**Clause ②: yes** — path limb (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`); content limb yes: new keys on a published schema / accept-set widening. Draft; `needs:contract-review` is attached to this PR and to the card in the same stroke. Not flipped to ready by this seat — the contract review clears it.

Maintainer ruling 2026-09-01 (director batch 22, verbatim 「同意」; card comment 5494341350), quoted untranslated:

> **裁定内容**:行级 action 获得 `bulkActionDefs` 的声明式对应物 —— `operation: 'update'` + `patch`(+ `visible` 谓词),单记录、走数据面、**用调用者自己的权限**、钩子与校验照常触发、`undoable` 有锚点。键形细节(在 `ActionType` 加成员还是并列键形、与既有 action 词表的混用规则)由实施 PR 设计并在正文钉死供复审。

This is the **spec half only**, contract-first. The executor halves — the runtime action dispatcher and the objectui row-action executor — are downstream cards the spec seat files at ACCEPT with `Blocked-by:` lines on #14092; until they land both keys are `planned` in the liveness ledger and an authored update action fails loudly at click (it reaches the platform action route with no handler), never silently.

## What lands

`ActionSchema` (registered actions — standalone in `stack.actions` or embedded on an object) gains, mirroring `bulk-action.zod.ts` word for word and inventing no second spelling:

| key | shape | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `operation` | `'update'` (one member) | the declarative single-record field write |
| `patch` | `Record of string to unknown`, optional | static field values written to the current record, merged UNDER the values `params` collects (a param of the same name wins); passed through verbatim |

Reused, nothing duplicated: the action's own `params` (the dialog), `visible` (per-record predicate), `confirmText` (param-less form only — the #7428 pair rule composes unchanged) and `undoable`, which now has its anchor: the patch names exactly the fields whose prior values are captured.

The card's `duly` shape parses on an object-embedded action and on a standalone action that names `objectName`:

```ts
{ name: 'duly_task_complete', label: 'Complete', operation: 'update', patch: { status: 'done' },
  visible: 'record.status == "open" || record.status == "in_progress"' }
```

## Key shape — designed here, pinned for the contract reviewer

**(a) Parallel key, not an `ActionType` member.** `operation` sits beside `type`; `type` keeps its materialized default `'script'`. Read them as route and verb: `type` answers WHERE the action dispatches — `'script'` is the platform action route (`POST /api/v1/actions/OBJECT/ACTION`, the route objectui's `executeScript` already posts to with the record id and the collected params) — and `operation` answers WHAT the platform does there. Three reasons, in order of weight:

1. It is the ruling's own spelling and the bulk def's: `{ operation: 'update', patch, visible }` copies across surfaces unchanged. A `type: 'update'` member would be a second spelling of the same intent.
2. objectui types `ActionRunner.builtinExecutors` as `Record of RunnableActionType`, deliberately, so a member added to `ActionType` stops the console compiling until an executor exists — objectui's designed Tier-2 guard. The pin gate injects this tree's spec into the console bundle only (a Vite resolver on the `import` condition), so a member would not red the gate today, but it would hard-block objectui's next spec bump on the executor card. The contract-first split (spec now, halves downstream, in any order) must not carry that coupling; with the parallel key the console bumps freely and the update action degrades to a loud click-time failure until its half lands.
3. It needs the smallest change to the existing `type`-keyed rules: one carve-out in the #2169 script-executability refinement (`body`-less, `target`-less is the legal shape here). Every other rule composes: the `onSuccess` and `newTabUrl` rules see `type: 'script'` and defer to the block below.

The alternative — `ActionType` gains `'update'` — was measured and is the line to change if review prefers it: one enum member, `TARGET_REQUIRED_TYPES` excludes it, the same refusal table keyed on `type === 'update'`, plus a refusal on `InlineActionSchema` (it picks `type`) and on `DashboardHeaderActionSchema` (`WidgetActionTypeSchema` derives from `ActionType` by that file's doctrine). Its benefit is one discriminator per surface and no default-materialization asymmetry; its cost is reason 2. Recorded in the report's `open_questions`.

**Consequence to know, stated rather than hidden:** an explicitly authored `type: 'script'` beside `operation: 'update'` is accepted — at object level a materialized `.default()` is indistinguishable from an authored value (the asymmetry #13897 recorded for its `.default(false)` keys), and it means the same thing. The parsed shape is therefore always `{ type: 'script', operation: 'update', patch }`; **executors check `operation` before `type`.**

**(b) Exclusivity — one refusal per combination, at the contradicting key, `code: 'custom'`, first sentence names the executor the key belongs to** (`refuseDeclarativeUpdateContradictions` in `action.zod.ts`):

| beside `operation: 'update'` | path | why |
|---|---|---|
| any explicit `type` other than `'script'` (`url` · `modal` · `flow` · `api` · `form`) | `type` | those dispatch on `target` (`api` makes the browser call the endpoint itself); none performs the write |
| `target` | `target` | names a handler / URL / page / flow / endpoint — the update dispatches on none |
| `body` | `body` | the inline handler of a script action; the write IS the patch (carved out of the #4352 rule so the author gets this message, not "a non-script action dispatches on target") |
| `method` · `bodyExtra` · `bodyShape` · `recordIdParam` · `recordIdField` | each | the `type: 'api'` transport family: no request, no request body, the record is bound from context |
| `onSuccess` | `onSuccess` | its `result` scope is a handler's return value; not defined for the declarative write yet (reversible: refuse now, define later) |
| `opensInNewTab` · `newTabUrl` | each | the handler-redirect channel; no handler |
| `locations` containing `list_toolbar` | `locations.N` | no current record there — the selection bar is the bulk def's home |

`type: 'update'` (the member spelling) is refused on the enum with the prescription pointing at `operation`; `operation: 'delete'` / `'custom'` are refused with the reason (a row delete is the object's own affordance and was not ruled; `custom` on a def means "dispatch the action this def NAMES" — on a row the action is already the action). The bulk def's `op` shorthand and `values` / `set` / `update` rename onto `operation` / `patch` in the unknown-key message.

**(c) Presence.** `patch` without `operation: 'update'` is refused at `patch` (it would be silently dropped — ADR-0078). `operation: 'update'` with neither `patch` nor a non-empty `params` is refused at `patch` (nothing to write). Params-only (the dialog supplies the values) and both (patch under params) are legal.

**(d) `objectName`.** The same schema parses an embedded action (object implicit) and a standalone one, so the schema cannot judge it; `defineStack`'s cross-reference walk can, and does (`collectGlobalUpdateActionErrors` in `stack.zod.ts`): a standalone `operation: 'update'` action with no `objectName` is refused — a global action has no current record — with the two spellings that work (`objectName`, or embed it on the object). Runs before the object-count early return, like the duplicate-key check beside it.

**(e) `undoable`.** Keeps its describe sentence ("single-record update actions only") and gains the anchor: `operation: 'update'` is the declared form of that action; the patch names exactly the fields whose prior values are captured.

**Deliberately not refused:** `resultDialog`, `successMessage`, `errorMessage`, `refreshAfter`, `requiredPermissions` (the platform action route enforces it server-side — the describe's claim stays true on this route), `ai` exposure (the MCP path is the same route), `record_related` (which record binds there is the executor's call, as for script actions today). **Inline page-element actions** cannot carry the keys: `InlineActionSchema` picks neither, so its strict shape refuses them as unknown — pinned. `DashboardHeaderActionSchema` is untouched (`ActionType` did not move).

**Beyond the dispatch brief's minimum list (target / method / bodyExtra / other types) — derived judgements for review:** the `bodyShape` / `recordIdParam` / `recordIdField` / `onSuccess` / `opensInNewTab` / `newTabUrl` refusals, the `list_toolbar` refusal, the `body` carve-out message, and the stack-level `objectName` rule. Each is the reversible direction (refuse now, allow later is additive).

## Executor contract — for the runtime and objectui cards

1. **Read `operation` before `type`.** An action with `operation: 'update'` is the declarative single-record field write; its `type` is `'script'` (the route) and carries no handler.
2. **Single-record, data-plane, as the caller.** The platform action route performs ONE update of the CURRENT record (the `recordId` the route already receives) on the object the action belongs to (its embedding object, or `objectName`) through the data plane under the caller's own identity — never system-elevated. This consumes the #14010 ruling's direction (`runAs: 'user'` = pinned to the triggering user) and does not reopen it; no `runAs` key is added here.
3. **Permissions, hooks, validations fire exactly as for a user edit.** A caller who cannot read or write the row is refused with a located error — the #14143 class (a swallowed load must never become an implicit grant); `requiredPermissions` stays enforced on the route.
4. **The write is `{ ...patch, ...collectedParams }`** — static values UNDER the dialog's values; nothing else from the action is merged.
5. **`undoable: true`** captures the prior values of exactly the fields written and offers the Undo affordance the existing readers already implement.
6. **`visible`** is evaluated with the current record bound, fail-closed, as today; it is a UI gate, not authorization (point 3 is the authorization).
7. **objectui:** forward `operation` / `patch` off the schema where `bodyExtra` is forwarded today (the action-button forward list), dispatch on `operation` before `type`, and amend the two ledger entries to `live` citing the reads. Until then the action reaches the route on the script path and gets the route's loud refusal.

## Not touched

`bulk-action.zod.ts` (mirrored, not moved); the `method` docblock region of `action.zod.ts` with the `/api/v1/sys_api_key/{id}` example — #14093 owns it, serialized behind this card, and the diff leaves those lines byte-identical; `packages/runtime`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/rest`, `packages/lint`; objectui; `content/docs/releases`; `skills`. #14143 is not addressed here (it landed on its own card). #14010 remains as ruled.

## Semver and changeset

`@objectstack/spec` **minor** (`.changeset/action-row-update-declarative.md`) — a pure widening: `operation` and `patch` were unknown keys on this strict shape, every new refusal is keyed on one of them, and the one edited existing rule only gains a carve-out. Nothing that parsed before stops parsing.

Also in the diff: `packages/spec/liveness/action.json` (two `planned` entries with `authorWarn` + `authorHint` naming the executor halves, evidence anchored on the two named symbols), `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` (the hand-written narrative gains the declarative write; the "complete enum" sentence stays true), and the regenerated `content/docs/references/**` and `liveness/state-counts.md` (`check:generated --fix` proved exactly those two stale).

- Gate derivation: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` inside the worktree at `44e26d67` names **78** commands (68 by path + 7 by change kind + 5 whole-tree, 2 shared). All 78 run, exit captured before any pipe: **71 exit 0**; **7 NOT MEASURED** by their own verdict text (prerequisite: the rest of the workspace is not built here / no test log) — `check-dev-prereqs`, `check-test-completeness` (exit 3, "record this gate as NOT MEASURED"), lint `check:doc-formula-expressions` and `check:doc-security-posture` (exit 3, `@objectstack/formula` / `@objectstack/lint` dist absent), spec `check:skill-examples` (client-react dist absent; the one fence this diff adds carries no `os:check` marker, so it is outside that gate's population either way), `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3), `check:type-check-debt` (exit 3). CI builds the closure first and owns those readings. Among the 71: `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:export-origins`, `check:llms-txt`, `check:skill-refs`, `check:strictness-ledger`, `check:variant-docs`, `check:yaml-examples`, `check:spec-parsed-alias`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:merge-driver`, `check:published-files`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check-closing-keyword-parity`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check:engine-double-contract`.
- eslint: targeted, `eslint --no-inline-config` over the three edited TypeScript files — 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` scan was not run here (CI's).
- **Reverse verification** (fix committed first; pin file imports `./action.zod` / `../stack.zod` from src, so no dist is in the loop; restore = `git checkout HEAD -- absolute-path` under an EXIT/INT/TERM trap; each restore proven by `git hash-object` equal to the HEAD blob `c21a6e06…` and an empty `git diff HEAD`; final tree clean):
